transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Veridian - Head of Security), Elise Montoya (Veridian - Legal Counsel), Priya Shah (Veridian - Platform Eng)

Summary (auto):
Quick legal + security review focused on key question: who holds keys, where processing happens, and what subprocessor commitments Red wood can make for EU/US patient data. Customer wants clear options (hosted with region pinning, dedicated pools, or private deployment) and a path for proofs for procurement.

Topics: KMS custody options, region pinning mechanics, subprocessor list and flow, SOC 2/ISO evidence, audit logs and retention, SSO/SAML and RBAC, cross-border failover expectations.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account. We have Jordan, our solutions engineer, with me. How are you all?
[00:06] Samir: Good, thanks. Samir here. A bit pressed for time so hopefully we can get to the K M S bits early.
[00:10] Elise: Hi all. Elise, legal. We'll want the subprocessor commitments and DPA language.
[00:14] Priya: Priya from platform, hi. We're mainly concerned about custody and cross-border processing for EU records.
[00:18] Jordan: Great, thanks. Agenda: run through the three deployment options briefly — hosted with region pinning, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC or on-prem). Then dive into KMS custody and audit log posture.
[00:25] Samir: Sounds good. Quick qualifier: are you able to support region-affinity for EU-only processing and guarantee no egress to US unless we flip a toggle?
[00:33] Maya: Short answer: yes, we offer region pinning for hosted models, and you can also opt for Dedicated or Private for stronger guarantees. There's nuance — for example, in hosted we do automated routing with region affinity but certain background services & backups may touch other regions unless you choose Private.
[00:46] Elise: What's the exact language we can put in a contract? We need something procurement/legal can read without ambiguity.
[00:51] Jordan: For contract language we typically offer a region-affinity clause that says primary processing will be in the elected region and that subprocessor locations are listed in the subprocessor appendix. For absolute physical isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[01:00] Samir: And KMS? Our policy says we need customer-managed keys for EU PHI. Can Redwood bring-your-own-key for hosted?
[01:07] Maya: We have three KMS options: Redwood-managed keys (default), customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (we call it BYOK), and a KMS-escrow option for Private deployments. BYOK is available for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we support BYOK for enterprise customers but it requires enrollment and some networking/identity setup.
[01:24] Priya: Wait — when you say BYOK for hosted, is the key material exported to Redwood or do you keep it in our KMS?
[01:30] Jordan: Good question. With cloud-KMS BYOK, key material stays in your cloud KMS; Redwood requests crypto operations via an IAM role and never holds the plaintext private key. There are edge cases — e.g., some HSM-backed workflows we coordinate for cross-region failover.
[01:43] Elise: So legally we need to confirm Redwood never 'has' the keys. Is there an attestation or docs?
[01:48] Maya: We can provide an architecture diagram and a KMS whitepaper that describes custody boundaries. We also include details in the DPA appendix. We'll attach the whitepaper to the follow-up.
[01:56] Samir: About cross-border processing: if a user in EU hits the service and your router can't find capacity in EU for a burst, what's the fallback? We can't have content leave the EU without explicit approval.
[02:06] Jordan: By default our smart routing will prioritize regional capacity and try elastic burst within the same region or compatible model variants. For enterprise customers with strict residency, we offer strict region-pinning where requests will queue or fail rather than failover to a different jurisdiction. That is a Dedicated/Private option in most cases.
[02:21] Priya: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs with retention of seven years and tamper-evidence for our auditors.
[02:28] Jordan: We emit request-level audit logs, including token usage, model version, timestamp, route, and end-point. For hosted we retain logs according to plan — we can set retention windows and export to your log sink (e.g., Splunk or BigQuery). For tamper evidence, we support signed log streams and cryptographic integrity checks for Dedicated/Private.
[02:45] Elise: Do you provide SOC 2 + ISO 27001 certs? We need to see copies, plus evidence of regular penetration testing.
[02:50] Maya: Yes, Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we will share cert bundles and recent pen test summaries through a secure link.
[02:58] Samir: One more — subprocessors. We need to know which data plane subprocessors you use in EU and US and their roles. Also how you do notification for changes.
[03:07] Maya: We have an up-to-date subprocessor list that we publish; for customers with contractual requirements we can provide a snapshot at signing. We also offer a 30-day notice for subprocessor additions and an escape clause for critical changes.
[03:18] Elise: Can you commit to advance notice and a right to object?
[03:21] Maya: Yes — standard language is 30 days' notice and a right to object with remedies.
[03:25] Priya: Practical item: if we pick hosted with region pinning and enable BYOK, do we need a VPC peering or private link to avoid any cross-tenant traffic touching public internet?
[03:35] Jordan: For BYOK and strong isolation we recommend either dedicated VPC peering (Private) or use of PrivateLink / Private Endpoint for hosted enterprise. We can diagram the network flows.
[03:43] Samir: How do you handle backups and cold storage — do those copies stay in-region? We can't accept backups leaving the EU.
[03:49] Jordan: Backups are regionally stored by default. If you require strict in-region backup, we can guarantee that with a Private or Dedicated contract; hosted default has regional backup controls but some metadata services might be multi-region unless locked down.
[04:02] Elise: On SSO and RBAC — we use SAML and SCIM for automated provisioning and strict role separation. How does Redwood map roles for audit?
[04:10] Maya: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is customizable — you can map SAML groups to Redwood roles, and admin actions are logged for audit. We also have token-scoped API keys and can bind keys to projects and retention policies.
[04:22] Priya: Does your logging include redaction options for sensitive fields? Our dataset includes PHI; we may need to redact or pseudonymize before logging.
[04:30] Jordan: We support configurable log redaction and can apply pre-ingest pseudonymization rules; however, if you request full plaintext logging we need contractual approvals. For PHI we usually recommend pseudonymization at the client side or use Private deployment with strict retention.
[04:44] Samir: There is also legal interest in legal process — if law enforcement requests data, where is the disclosure processed and who's notified?
[04:52] Elise: Yep. We need a clear notification process.
[04:54] Maya: We publish a transparency report and will notify customers per the DPA and local laws. For Private deployments where you manage the control plane, you have more direct control over disclosures.
[05:05] Samir: For procurement, we need a plug-and-play set of options to present to risk committee: "option A: hosted + region affinity + BYOK with private endpoints (recommended), option B: Dedicated reserved capacity with BYOK, option C: Private on-prem." Can you codify that?
[05:17] Maya: Absolutely — we'll send a one-pager that maps those options to legal and security guarantees.
[05:21] Elise: Also need SLAs for data residency and for key availability. If BYOK keys are in our KMS, failure there impacts decrypt. What's your recommended HA pattern?
[05:30] Jordan: We recommend multi-region KMS configuration with replication if allowed by your policy, or an HSM-backed KMS for high availability. For strict residency, you'd pick a geo-replicated KMS within the EU and choose Dedicated/Private routing to stay within region. We can include recommended HA patterns in the architecture doc.
[05:46] Priya: For the pilot we'd like to run a small proof: 1) verify region-pin routing under load, 2) verify KMS calls never return key material to Redwood, 3) audit log export. Are you okay with that?
[05:58] Jordan: Yes, we can scope a short pilot. We'll need sample traffic and acceptance criteria from you.
[06:04] Samir: How long does the onboarding for BYOK in hosted take?
[06:07] Maya: Typically 2-4 weeks, depends on networking and legal review. Dedicated/Private onboarding can take longer.
[06:12] Elise: We'll want contract language on key custody and a kill-switch clause — ability to revoke keys and ensure data becomes inaccessible.
[06:19] Jordan: If keys are BYOK in your KMS, revoking the key will make data inaccessible. We can include a kill-switch playbook in the DPA appendix.
[06:27] Maya: Recap of next steps: I will send the KMS whitepaper, subprocessor inventory snapshot, and a one-pager that maps the three options to guarantees. Jordan will draft pilot acceptance criteria and a short benchmark plan. Priya will provide traffic profile and residency constraints. Elise to confirm legal review timeline.
[06:43] Elise: We aim to get legal sign-off within two weeks after receipt of docs.
[06:47] Samir: Ok thanks all. Quick note — we've been evaluating BigCloudAI and NimbusServe; one reason we're talking to Redwood is that we like the clear options on physical isolation.
[06:58] Maya: Appreciate the transparency. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule the pilot kickoff for the week of Nov 23 if that works.
[07:04] Priya: Works for us. Thanks.
[07:06] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links.

End of transcript.
